title: The racket
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: The scholarship's reply deadline was yesterday. Wood hides out in the backroom and says the word 'racket' four times.

panels.composition: The frame shop backroom. WOOD cutting foam core, badly. A wall calendar with yesterday's date circled and then scribbled out.
props: wall calendar with a scribbled-out date

balloons.text: Art school is a commercial racket designed to castrate raw vision.

image.prompt: a young man cutting foam core with a dull utility knife in a framing backroom, a wall calendar behind him with one date circled and scribbled out, brush-pen black and white

panels.composition: The OWNER in the doorway, reading glasses.

image.prompt: a woman in reading glasses standing in a backroom doorway looking at a young man who is talking to foam core

panels.composition: Wood, the knife going through the foam core and into the table.

image.prompt: close-up of a utility knife driven through foam core and stuck into a wooden worktable

panels.composition: Wood pulling the knife out. The calendar. The circled date, scribbled, but the circle still visible under the scribble. It's drawn so the reader can see both.

image.prompt: a young man pulling a knife free from a table beside a wall calendar where a scribbled-out date still shows its circle underneath, black and white
image.notes: The scribble doesn't fully cover the circle. Both must read.

art.line: brush-pen over rough blue pencil; xerox grain; stark spotting; rain in frantic vertical hatching (Arc 1's aesthetic)

notes: The deadline passes off the page. The calendar is the only record.
